html:
SMTO-POL-0009 — This Skill is switched off for this task

GUID: 17fb10e4-f0b3-4f8b-98e9-687f5282018e
Slug: capability-scope
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • The Agent tried to use a Skill (a set of tools, such as Email or Files) that isn't allowed in this task's capability choices. None of that Skill's tools were used.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Next to the message box, select the Capabilities button and search for the Skill you need. The list shows whether that Skill is excluded for this prompt, this conversation or everywhere.
  2. If the Skill is set to Exclude (−), change it to Enable or Prefer, choose the place under Apply to, then select Apply. An excluded Skill is hidden from the Agent, so none of its tools can be used.
  3. Open Options next to the message box. If Automatic Capability Selection is switched off, make sure the Skill is one you picked, or switch it back on. With automatic selection off, the task can only use the Skills you picked.
  4. Send your request again as a new message. Capability changes apply to the next request, not to the task that already started.

What success looks like

  • The Agent uses the Skill's tools in the new task and this message doesn't appear.

If it still fails

  • If you can't change the Skill (for example it says 'Managed automatically') or it shows as unavailable, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Turning a Skill on doesn't change permissions on your computers; those are set separately.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Tool discovery returned capability_scope because the requested Skill (or Skill section) has no tools within the run's capability selection: it is excluded by the capability policy, missing from a manual selection, or not in enabled_skill_ids.

What this means

  • Discovery found no tools from the requested skill available within the run's scoped capability selection. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Discovery found no tools from the requested skill available within the run's scoped capability selection.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the skill's registered tools with the task selection and target availability; installation and permission are separate checks.

How to fix it

  • Compare the run's native_capability_policy (enabled, preferred and excluded skill IDs) and native_selected_skill_ids with the requested Skill in ToolCatalog.skill_tool_ids (native/catalog.py). Change the prompt, conversation or global Capabilities policy to include the Skill and start a new request; operating-system permissions are a separate control.
  • Select a permitted target or scope, or explicitly change the owning policy if intended. OS permissions are a separate control.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Discovery exposes at least one intended allowed tool from the requested skill in this run.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
